note: A gives the 'thrice great Hermes', the Egyptian identified with Thoth, the mythical namesake of Hermetic philosophy and a name used by Greek writers on philosophy and alchemy, but it does not say Hellenistic syncretism, author of the Hermetica, or founder of alchemy; B calls him 'Thrice-Greatest', living in Egypt, the discoverer of Alchemy and founder of Astrology, but leaves out the Hermes–Thoth syncretism, the Hermetica and natural philosophy.
